content.user_title: Build Azure Batch Workflows in Java
content.value_statement: Large-scale Java workloads require careful Azure Batch setup and lifecycle management. This skill provides focused SDK examples for clients, pools, jobs, tasks, nodes, schedules, and monitoring.
actual_capabilities: Configure synchronous and asynchronous Azure Batch clients with Entra ID or shared keys.
Create, inspect, resize, autoscale, and delete Azure Batch compute pools.
Create, list, monitor, terminate, and delete jobs and tasks.
Submit task collections and large task lists with Azure Batch SDK methods.
Retrieve task output, inspect nodes, reboot nodes, and obtain remote login settings.
Create recurring job schedules and handle Azure Batch service errors.
limitations: Examples target azure-compute-batch 1.0.0-beta.5 and may require changes for newer versions.
A configured Azure Batch account, pool, subscription, credentials, and permissions are required.
The skill does not provision complete Azure infrastructure or validate quotas, permissions, costs, and regional availability.
Task command strings require operating-system validation and trusted inputs before production use.

use_cases.title: Integrate Batch Processing
use_cases.description: Add Azure Batch client, job, and task operations to a Java service.

use_cases.title: Operate Compute Pools
use_cases.description: Create, resize, autoscale, inspect, and remove pools supporting repeatable workloads.

use_cases.title: Run Parallel Workloads
use_cases.description: Submit many tasks, monitor progress, retrieve output, and manage scheduled execution.

prompt_templates.title: Connect a Java Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to create a synchronous Azure Batch Java client using Entra ID and AZURE_BATCH_ENDPOINT.

prompt_templates.title: Submit a Batch Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Java workflow that creates a job on an existing pool and submits fifty independent tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Scale and Monitor a Pool
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Java approach for autoscaling an Azure Batch pool, monitoring task counts, and handling long-running operations.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Resilient Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a production Java Batch workflow with schedules, retries, time limits, task output collection, error handling, and cleanup.

output_examples.input: Create a Java client with recommended authentication.
output: Use DefaultAzureCredential with the configured Azure Batch endpoint.
Build a synchronous Batch client and avoid embedding account secrets.

output_examples.input: Submit one thousand independent tasks to an existing job.
output: Prepare uniquely identified task definitions with validated command strings.
Use the large-task submission method and monitor task counts until completion.

output_examples.input: Reduce costs for a fault-tolerant workload.
output: Combine dedicated and low-priority nodes based on interruption tolerance.
Enable autoscale and set job time limits, retry limits, and progress monitoring.

best_practices: Prefer Entra ID and managed identities over shared account keys.
Set wall-clock limits and retry limits for every production workload.
Monitor long-running operations, task counts, exit codes, and output before cleanup.
anti_patterns: Do not concatenate untrusted input into Batch task command strings.
Do not embed account keys, endpoints, pool identifiers, or job identifiers in source control.
Do not delete pools or jobs before collecting required task output and diagnostics.

faq.question: Which Azure Java package does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers com.azure:azure-compute-batch, with examples based on version 1.0.0-beta.5.

faq.question: Can it create Azure Batch pools?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows pool creation, inspection, resizing, autoscaling, and deletion through the Batch client.

faq.question: Which authentication methods are shown?
faq.answer: It shows recommended Entra ID authentication and an alternative shared-key configuration.

faq.question: Can it submit many tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers task collections and the large-task submission method.

faq.question: Does it provision an Azure subscription or Batch account?
faq.answer: No. The subscription, Batch account, pool, credentials, and permissions must already exist.

faq.question: Does it support monitoring and troubleshooting?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers task counts, states, exit codes, output files, node details, and Batch service errors.
